title: The Lament and the Hope
subtitle: The prophet grieves before he promises, and promises only because grief is not the last word.

sections.title: Why We Lament
sections.body:
We have been taught that the strong believer does not complain. That a settled faith goes quiet under suffering and waits with a closed mouth. The Bible teaches no such thing. A third of the Psalms are complaints addressed straight to God, and the man after God's own heart wrote most of them. Lament is not the failure of faith. It is one of its oldest languages.

To lament is to refuse two lies at once. It refuses the lie that the wound does not matter, and it refuses the lie that God is not listening. The one who shrugs at injustice has stopped believing the world was made good. The one who grieves in silence, addressing no one, has stopped believing there is anyone on the throne. The lamenter does the harder, truer thing. He carries the wound directly to the God who could have prevented it, and he says so.

Walter Brueggemann called these the Psalms of disorientation, and he was right to insist the church needs them. A faith that can only praise is a faith that has not yet met the world. We did not invent our griefs, and we will not be healed by pretending them away. So we say the hard sentence out loud. How long, O Lord. The asking is already a kind of trust.

sections.title: The Discipline of Confession
sections.body:
There is a grief that points outward at the injustice of others, and there is a harder grief that turns and looks at the church in the mirror. The prophets did both. They named the sins of the nations, and then they named the sins of the people of God, and they did not soften the second to protect the household. Confession is lament that has stopped looking for someone else to blame.

Daniel prayed for a people whose exile he had not caused, and he did not pray as an innocent man standing apart from guilty men. He said we have sinned. Nehemiah did the same, confessing the sins of his fathers and of himself in the same breath, refusing the distance that would have kept his own hands clean. This is the pattern Scripture gives us. The one who intercedes for the church stands inside the church's sin, not above it. We covered for the abuser. We baptized our prejudices and called them conviction. We loved our comfort more than our neighbor. We did this.

Confession is not despair, and it is not performance. It is the plain naming of what is true so that mercy has something real to forgive. A church that will not confess cannot be cleansed, because it keeps insisting there is nothing to cleanse. So we say it honestly, by name, without the cushion of the passive voice. Then we wait for the mercy that has never once failed to come to the honest.

sections.title: The Vision of Shalom
sections.body:
Prophecy that stops at the indictment curdles into cynicism, and cynicism has never repaired anything. The prophets refused to stop there. After the charge and after the grief came the promise, and the promise was not a vague comfort but a concrete picture of the world made whole. They swing their hammers at swords until the swords become plows. They sit every man under his own vine with no one left to make him afraid.

Isaiah saw the wolf lie down with the lamb and the whole earth full of the knowledge of God as the waters cover the sea. John saw the holy city come down and heard the voice say that God will wipe away every tear, and death will be no more, and the old order of grief will have passed. This is shalom. Not the absence of conflict only, but the presence of everything as it was meant to be. The hungry fed, the prisoner freed, the broken mended, the dead raised. The world is not abandoned. It is being made new.

This hope is not a sedative. It does not excuse us from the work by promising the work will be done over our heads. It is the opposite. The vision of the world set right is precisely what gives us the nerve to labor for it now, knowing our labor is not in vain. We do not build the kingdom, but we are not permitted to ignore it either. We plant under a sky we trust, for a harvest we may not live to see. The tears are real. They are also numbered, and they are also ending.

prayers.title: How Long, O Lord
prayers.text: How long, O Lord, will the violent prosper and the gentle be ground down. We have seen the blood of the innocent and we have no words equal to it. Do not hide your face from the cry of the afflicted. Rise up, O God, and let the earth know that you have not forgotten the poor.

prayers.title: For Those Who Suffer in Silence
prayers.text: Father, we bring you the ones whose grief has no audience, the abused who were not believed and the mourners no one came to sit with. You keep their tears in your bottle and you write their sorrows in your book. Be near to the brokenhearted tonight, for you are close to them in a way we cannot be. Hold the ones we could not reach.

prayers.title: Over an Unjust World
prayers.text: O God of justice, the scales of this world are bent and the strong have rigged them. We are weary of waiting while the wicked call evil good and are praised for it. We do not understand your patience and we will not pretend that we do. Yet we bring our anger to you and not to despair, and we ask you to set right what we cannot.

prayers.title: For the Sins of the Church
prayers.text: Lord, we confess the sins of your people as our own, for we have not stood apart from them. We sheltered the powerful and turned from the wounded, and we called our silence peace. We have loved our reputation more than your righteousness. Have mercy on us, and do not deal with us as our cowardice deserves.

prayers.title: We Did This
prayers.text: Merciful God, we have blamed the world for darkness while the lamp in our own hands went out. We covered for the guilty, we wearied of the needy, and we made our comfort into a doctrine. We did this, and we will not hide behind the passive voice before you. Cleanse us, and teach us to be the kind of people who confess before we are caught.

prayers.title: Swords Into Plowshares
prayers.text: God of peace, we hold to your promise that the weapons of war will be beaten into the tools of harvest. Hasten the day when no one studies war anymore and every person rests unafraid. Until that morning comes, make us its early signs, planting and mending in a world still learning to trust you. We wait for your kingdom, and we work while we wait.

prayers.title: Every Tear Wiped Away
prayers.text: Father, you have promised a day when you will wipe away every tear from every eye, when death will be no more and mourning and crying and pain will have passed away. We take you at your word over the evidence of the grave. Comfort us now with the end you have written, and let the hope of it steady our hands. The old order is passing, and you are making all things new.

prayers.title: The Earth Full of His Knowledge
prayers.text: O Lord, we long for the day the whole earth is filled with the knowledge of your glory as the waters cover the sea. We believe the wolf will lie down with the lamb and the nursing child will play unharmed. Plant that future in us so deeply that cynicism cannot take root. Come quickly, and find us laboring for the world you have promised to make whole.
